I'm planning a complex trip that involves three legs (Seattle to Chicago, then Chicago to London with a 6-hour layover that I want to use to visit family in the city, then London to a customer site in Munich), and I want to combine business travel reimbursement with personal extension days. My questions: (1) do the personal vacation days during the layover count as breaking continuity of business travel for per-diem purposes; (2) can I keep the corporate rate on the hotel for the personal night between the conference and the customer visit; (3) is there a difference in policy depending on whether I'm a manager or an individual contributor; (4) what about meals on the personal day — am I excluded entirely or just reduced; (5) if my spouse joins me for the weekend in London, can I expense the hotel difference between single and double occupancy. Please cite the policy section for each answer.

Detailed scenario: I attended an industry conference last week. The conference fee was paid by my employer. While there I had three customer dinners that totaled $620, a hotel stay of 4 nights at $410/night (over the $300 NYC cap), an Uber to and from the airport totaling $190, a rebooking fee of $150 because my return flight was cancelled and I had to fly the next morning, a hotel for the unplanned extra night of $295, breakfast on the extra morning of $24, and a $40 airport meal. I need to know which of these are reimbursable, which require pre-approval (and from whom), which I need to split with the customer for tax purposes, and whether the over-cap nights need an exception request or if the cancellation justifies them automatically.
